name: Togarmah
overview: Togarmah is a male figure mentioned in the Bible as the son of Gomer. Beyond this genealogical note, Scripture provides no additional details about his tribe or personal attributes. His mention is brief and primarily serves a genealogical purpose within the biblical record.
namesAndTitles: The name Togarmah appears as a proper name in Genesis 10:3. There is no specific meaning or divine origin attributed to his name in the biblical text, so it is understood simply as a personal name without additional connotation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Togarmah as the son of Gomer, establishing a direct familial link. No other family relationships or tribal affiliations are documented in the biblical text beyond this father-son connection.
scriptureSignificance: Togarmah's significance lies in his place within the genealogical framework of Genesis 10:3, which traces the descendants of Noah's sons. As a son of Gomer, Togarmah contributes to the biblical account of the nations' origins, highlighting God's sovereign plan in populating the earth through distinct family lines. His mention underscores the importance of lineage in understanding the historical and theological context of Scripture.
